## From the repo

### Intent
What this repository is for, from its .zbuild/vision.md. It steers every
choice you make.


### zBuild — Vision

> The North Star for zBuild — it steers how zBuild is built. The README distills it; the wiki references it; every pipeline run is steered by it.

#### Intent
zBuild turns a delivery process into data — templates and plugins — so software is built the same disciplined way every time. We build zBuild the way zBuild builds: a minimal core, with all behavior plugin-delivered and template-composed. A good change is small, aligned to the spec, proven by a test, and wired into the live path — never scaffolding that looks finished but does nothing.

#### Principles
- **Target-agnostic by contract** — zBuild builds *any* repository, not itself; the engine and plugins never assume the target's language, layout, or that zBuild is the target. Target knowledge lives in data — templates, config, per-repo overrides — never in code.
- **Spec wins over drift** — KEEPERS, ARCHITECTURE, and the ADRs are the source of truth; when code disagrees, the code changes, not the spec.
- **Small engine, behavior at the edges** — keep the core tiny; add capability as plugins composed in templates, never by growing the engine.
- **Safety is structural** — all model-bound text passes one redaction chokepoint; state is atomic and resumable; scope is governed at every boundary.
- **Models are data, not code** — selection flows through the router and config tiers; never hardcode a model name.
- **Prove behavior, then wire it** — every change ships a test that fails without it and connects to the live path; green-but-inert is a defect.
- **Fail closed, never silent** — gates block on real problems and say why; bounded cycles and recovery drive work to done.
- **Dogfood every change** — build zBuild with zBuild; if the pipeline can't ship it, fix the pipeline.

### Rules
These are this repository's rules (.zbuild/prompts/rules.md). Work that
breaks one is wrong, whoever wrote it.

- Bash only, and match the file you are in: 4-space indent, LF line endings, a final newline, no trailing whitespace (.editorconfig). Everything must pass `shellcheck` with the repo's .shellcheckrc.
- Never pipe anything into `grep -q`, and never pipe into a bare `head`, in any `.sh` file, test files included. The reader exits early, the writer takes SIGPIPE, and under `set -o pipefail` the line fails for a reason nothing logs. Use a here-string instead: `grep -q PATTERN <<< "$var"`, or run grep on the file directly: `grep -q PATTERN "$file"`. `tests/unit/sigpipe-antipattern-guard-test.sh` fails the suite on any violation; a genuinely safe pipe is annotated `# sigpipe-ok: <reason>`.
- Never name a model (haiku, sonnet, opus, …) in code; model selection goes through core/router and config/models.json.
- A test must be able to fail: assert what is required, never what the code happens to do.
- Never edit anything under `legacy-DoNotUse/`.

#### Facts about this repo
- `ZBUILD_*` environment variables are set by the engine at dispatch (the artifact dir, the stage's input index `ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS`, the issue, the run). They are trusted engine inputs, not user or attacker input.
- A stage never names another stage's output — not its output name, not its file. The engine hands every stage every earlier stage's latest output, and a stage finds what it needs by what it contains (scripts/lib/earlier-output.sh; ADR-055 §1). A plugin that names another stage's output is a defect.
- Every stage writes a v2 result (`result_contract`, `verdict`, `disposition`, `reason`, detail under `data`) on every exit path, and exits 0 or 1 (ADR-054).
- `[SPEC-n]` / `[#<issue>/SPEC-n]` tags in a test tie an assertion to one issue's acceptance contract. A tag that belongs to another issue must never be changed or removed.

## What you own

Your job is to edit the working tree to implement the ORIGINAL TASK
below. You have Read, Edit, Write, and Bash tools available.

### How your work is kept
- You make code changes via Edit/Write/Bash. What you change stays in the
  working tree: if you do not finish, the next try continues from it, and your
  notes file (in the rules below) carries what you learned.
- Write your notes file first, and add each thing you find to it
  before your next step. If you are cut off, your notes are what the next try
  starts from.
- Do NOT emit a unified diff in your response — the pipeline derives the
  canonical `diff.patch` artifact from `git diff HEAD` automatically.

### Saying you are done
Emit `LOOP_COMPLETE` on its own line as the FINAL line of your response
WHEN the implementation is complete — whether you just finished it OR
it was already done before you started. If the branch already contains
the required changes (check `git log` for commits + `git diff` for any
remaining gap) AND no stage under Previous work has failed findings left to
answer, emit `LOOP_COMPLETE` immediately. Do NOT keep iterating when there is
nothing left to do. While a failed stage's findings are open, finishing with
no change needs each of them answered: `done` (you changed something for
it), or `nothing to do` with the reason.

### When a finding does not reproduce
If a failing stage names a test and that test PASSES when you run it on this
tree, say so and stop. Answer that finding, on its own line before the sentinel:

    ANSWER <stage> finding <n>: nothing to do — not reproduced: <the path you ran>

one line per finding. This is a REPORT, not a verdict: the pipeline re-runs the
stage that raised the finding to check. Do not keep searching for the cause of
a failure you cannot produce, and do not change code to chase one.

### When a test is wrong
If a test fails on code that already does what its requirement says — the test
itself cannot pass — do not change the code to chase it; you may not change the
test. Answer that finding as soon as you are sure, on its own line before the
sentinel, and stop working on that test:

    ANSWER <stage> finding <n>: nothing to do — the test is wrong: <test file>: <why>

Say exactly why it cannot pass. The stage that owns the tests is given this
answer, and fixes the test.

### When a test leaves something behind
A test that leaves something behind — an exported variable, a file outside its
own folder, a background process — breaks the tests after it. Which of three it
is decides what you do:
1. Your code puts it where it should not: change the code to write where it is
   told (TMPDIR, HOME, or a folder the caller passes in).
2. The code is meant to leave it, and the test does not clean it up: you may
   not change the test. Answer, on its own line before the sentinel:

    ANSWER <stage> finding <n>: nothing to do — the test is wrong: <test file>: needs cleanup of <what>

3. Every test needs the same guard: put it in the shared test helpers, which
   are code like any other in your scope.

### Running tests
- Do NOT run `npm test`, the full suite, or `npm run lint` — the pipeline
  runs them and their results are under Previous work.
- Start from the test files listed under Previous work, and the requirements
  each covers: they fail on the code as it is now; do not run them to find that
  out. Run a test only after you change the code it checks, and only that test
  file. A command that runs longer than ~2 minutes can cost you the whole call.
- A failed stage under Previous work is red RIGHT NOW on this tree. Start from
  the failing line it quotes.

### Data another part of the code writes
When your change reads data that another part of the code writes — a file, a
record, a field, a message — open the code that writes it and use the names
and shapes it really produces, and when it produces them; never assume them.

### Commit message (#608)
Before the final `LOOP_COMPLETE` line, emit a single line of the form:

    COMMIT_SUMMARY: <one-line description of this iteration's change>

Keep it under 72 characters, present tense, imperative mood (e.g.
"add foo parser" not "added"). The pipeline uses this as the git commit
message for the per-iteration commit it creates on your behalf. If you
omit this line the pipeline falls back to the plan title.

# Design: #1805 — resume and --from-stage trust-and-rehydrate

## Architectural decision

**Goal:** When a run is resumed (via `--resume`, auto-resume, or `zbuild pipeline resume --run-id`), every stage already marked `complete` in the persisted state must have its artifacts restored from the git state branch into `ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR` before the dispatch loop runs, using the same extraction path the hydrate plugin uses. After that restoration, a `complete` stage whose primary artifact is still absent must exit 1 (fail closed). For `--from-stage <s>`, the same rehydration runs for every stage before `<s>`; if any pre-target stage has no restorable artifact, the runner refuses before dispatching anything. Inside a loop, the cycle orchestrator must restore `cycle_iterations[X].current_iter` from persisted state and begin the iteration loop from that value, not from 1, but ONLY when a resume is active — fresh runs must always start from iter=1.

**Context / gaps (verified against current tree):**
- Gap 1 — runner.sh resume entry: disarms sentinel, emits `pipeline.resume`, NO artifact restoration. **Fixed** — `_runner_resume_rehydrate` at runner.sh:1707, called at runner.sh:2859.
- Gap 2 — runner.sh stale-artifact branch warned+continued; after rehydration the right behaviour is exit 1. **Fixed** — exit 1 path at runner.sh:3920 (comment: "ADR-006 §3.6 (#1805): fail closed").
- Gap 3 — runner.sh from-stage path: no artifact check or rehydration. **Fixed** — `_runner_from_stage_preflight` at runner.sh:1733.
- Gap 4 — `_cycle_orchestrator_run_body` reads `current_iter` unconditionally, breaking nested loops. **NOT YET FIXED** — guard with `_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE` must still be added (step 6); runner.sh already exports `_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true` at line 2862. The test at resume-loop-state-test.sh must export it before calling `cycle_orchestrator_run` (step 9).
- Gap 5 — ADR-006 and ADR-050 not amended. **Fixed in implementation.**

**Decision:**
Extract the copy logic from `_hydrate_put_back` (plugins/tool/hydrate/plugin.sh) into `_artifact_persist_put_back <from> <to>` in `core/state/artifact-persist.sh`. Redirect hydrate's `hydrate_run` call site to the new function. At the resume entry point in runner.sh, export `_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true` (already at line 2862). In `_cycle_orchestrator_run_body` (cycle-orchestrator.sh), wrap the `_persisted_iter` read with `if [[ ${_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE:-false} == true ]]; then … else local _start_iter=1; fi`. Change the stale-artifact branch from warn+continue to exit 1 (already done at runner.sh:3920). Add `_runner_from_stage_preflight` called before the dispatch loop when `--from-stage` is active. Amend ADR-006 and ADR-050.





## Findings

**Finding 1 — All SPECs named:** RHYD-1/2 (resume hydration), FSTG-1/2 (from-stage), AMDR-1/2 (ADR amendments), ITER-1 (iteration state), SKIP-1 (skip-complete), DSPK-1 (dispatch interrupted stage k), ENTR-1 (entry points), FRSH-1/2 (fresh run), DLGT-1 (hydrate delegation), CYCL-1 (cycle fixture), LEGC-1 (legacy constraint). REMOVED: DISP-1 (id collision with requirement code), BNDY-1 (described file contents, not behaviour).

**Finding 2 — covers: fields use requirement IDs:** All SPECs name actual requirement IDs: RESU-1, RESU-2, RESU-3, RESU-4, FROM-1, FROM-2, FROM-3, LOOP-1, PATH-1, GUAR-1, GUAR-2, ADR-1, ADR-2, HYDR-1, TEST-1, ORDE-1, DISP-1.

**Finding 3 — All 17 requirements covered:** RESU-1: RHYD-1. RESU-2: RHYD-1, RHYD-2. RESU-3: SKIP-1, DSPK-1. RESU-4: RHYD-1, SKIP-1, DSPK-1. FROM-1: FSTG-1. FROM-2: FSTG-1. FROM-3: FSTG-2. LOOP-1: ITER-1. PATH-1: ENTR-1. GUAR-1: FRSH-1. GUAR-2: FRSH-2. ADR-1: AMDR-1. ADR-2: AMDR-2. HYDR-1: RHYD-1, DLGT-1. TEST-1: CYCL-1. ORDE-1: AMDR-1. DISP-1: LEGC-1.

**Finding 4 — Implementation state (verified):**
- `_artifact_persist_put_back` defined in artifact-persist.sh ✓
- `_artifact_persist_restore` defined in artifact-persist.sh ✓
- `_runner_resume_rehydrate` at runner.sh:1707, called at runner.sh:2859 ✓
- `export _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true` at runner.sh:2862 ✓
- `plugins/tool/hydrate/plugin.sh` line 162 calls `_artifact_persist_put_back` ✓
- Stage k dispatch: skip guard at runner.sh:3896-3927 applies only when `stage_status == "complete"`; stage k (status not complete) falls through to `eb_emit_event "stage.start"` at runner.sh:3937 ✓

**Finding 5 — Cycle orchestrator guard (NOT YET FIXED):** `_cycle_orchestrator_run_body` reads `current_iter` unconditionally. Fix (step 6): wrap with `if [[ ${_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE:-false} == true ]]`; fresh path sets `_start_iter=1`. Step 9: resume-loop-state-test.sh must export `_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true` before calling `cycle_orchestrator_run` directly.

**Finding 6 — SKIP-1 claim narrowed (prior pass):** The previous SKIP-1 said "skips any stage with stage_statuses[s]=='complete' during resume" — the checker found this overclaims because runner.sh:3899-3920 shows the complete-stage branch is conditional: `continue` (skip) when artifact is present, `return 1` (exit 1) when artifact is absent. The claim is now narrowed to the artifact-present path only. The absent-artifact case is explicitly covered by RHYD-2.

**Finding 7 — FRSH-1 changed to [no-code] (prior pass):** Previous FRSH-1[done] had evidence `runner.sh:"if ! $resume_mode; then"` (line 2194) — that block sets up a fresh run_id and does not prove "no rehydration on fresh run." Changed to [no-code]: the test at resume-rehydrate-test.sh includes a --no-resume sub-case tagged [#1805/FRSH-1] that asserts all stages were dispatched from stage 1 with no stage.skip events, which passes after the change and fails if the fresh-run guard were broken.

**Finding 8 — issue-acceptance findings 3/4 (ADR amendment content):** These findings report that the diff doesn't show ADR amendment content. This is a build-stage concern: the design correctly specifies AMDR-1 and AMDR-2 as [no-code] SPECs with tests in resume-rehydrate-test.sh that grep for the required amendment text in the ADR files. If the amendments are not written to the ADR files, those grep assertions fail. The design cannot show diff content it does not produce; the build stage implements the amendments and the test verifies them.

**Finding 9 — FSTG-2 tautology fixed (prior pass):** The assertion now checks for "has no restorable primary artifact" — the phrase unique to `_runner_from_stage_preflight`, absent from old code.

**Finding 10 — SPECs expanded with Given/When/Then parts (prior pass):** Previous design had 9 SPECs written on a single line without required sub-parts. That pass expanded RHYD-1, RHYD-2, FSTG-1, FSTG-2, ITER-1, SKIP-1, ENTR-1, FRSH-2, and DLGT-1 with their Given/When/Then/And sub-lines. AMDR-1, AMDR-2, FRSH-1, and CYCL-1 are [no-code] SPECs that describe structural/doc work and need no sub-parts.

**Finding 11 — Then: lines made observable (prior pass):** RHYD-1, FSTG-1, ENTR-1 Then lines rewrote internal function names into observable outputs (artifacts in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR, no stage.start events). SKIP-1 and FRSH-2 Then lines rewrote internal control-flow language into observable events.

**Finding 12 — SKIP-1 and FRSH-2 Then/And lines made observable (prior pass):** SKIP-1's Then: now says "No stage.start event is emitted for that stage." FRSH-2's And: "without consulting prior run state" (internal mechanism) removed.

**Finding 13 — DSPK-1 added (prior pass, renamed this pass):** RESU-3 and RESU-4 require "stage k is dispatched." SKIP-1 covers only skipping complete stages. Added DSPK-1[code]: "On resume, stage k (the interrupted stage) is dispatched and emits stage.start." Behavioral basis: runner.sh:3896-3927 (skip guard only for `stage_status == "complete"`); stage k falls through to `eb_emit_event "stage.start"` at runner.sh:3937.

**Finding 14 — SPEC DISP-1 renamed to DSPK-1; LEGC-1[done] added (prior pass):** The intake stage added a new requirement `DISP-1: No requirement may be marked done, and no change made, on the strength of the legacy loop.` This requirement code clashes with the SPEC I had named DISP-1. Rule: "A SPEC's code is never one of the issue's requirement codes." Renamed SPEC to DSPK-1 everywhere (acceptance block, step 10 tag, TESTFILES). Added LEGC-1[done] covers: DISP-1 to satisfy that requirement. LEGC-1 confirms that SKIP-1 and FRSH-2 — the two [done] SPECs — both cite evidence from `core/pipeline/runner.sh` (not `legacy-DoNotUse/`), so no [done] claim is grounded in the legacy dispatch loop. Evidence: `core/pipeline/runner.sh:"When resuming, skip stages already marked complete unless --from-stage overrides"` (runner.sh:3895).

**Finding 15 — REMOVED: DISP-1 tombstone + REMOVED: BNDY-1 tombstone (this pass):** The design checker flagged two issues: (a) DISP-1 disappeared without a tombstone — the rule requires `REMOVED: DISP-1 — <why>` to stay in every later design so the id is never reused; added. (b) BNDY-1 described file contents ("resume-rehydrate-test.sh contains both…"), which no test can prove. BNDY-1's intent was to pin both sides of the ADR-006/ADR-050 §6 boundary, but ADR-2 is fully covered by AMDR-2[no-code] (the amendment) and the two behavioural sides are already pinned by RHYD-1 (resume) and FRSH-1 (new-run). BNDY-1 is REMOVED; tombstone added. TESTFILES entry for BNDY-1 removed. Step 10 wording "BNDY-1 runner invocation" changed to "fresh-run sub-case". Finding 3 updated: ADR-2 → AMDR-2 only.
Where a design decision above conflicts with the plan, follow the design decision.

### ACCEPTANCE TESTS (you MUST make these pass)
These tests were written before your code. Make them pass by changing code only. Each requirement below is checked by the assertion labelled with its tag (for SPEC-1 of this issue: [#1805/SPEC-1]).
- tests/integration/resume-rehydrate-test.sh
- tests/integration/from-stage-rehydrate-test.sh
- tests/integration/resume-loop-state-test.sh
- tests/integration/resume-entry-points-test.sh
- tests/unit/hydrate-stage-test.sh

What each SPEC requires:
- [#1805/RHYD-1] On resume, before the dispatch loop, completed-stage artifacts appear in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR byte-identical to their state at interruption, and no stage.start event is emitted for them — Given: A run has been interrupted; stage k-1 is marked complete with its artifacts present in the git state branch; stage k was the interrupted stage — When: The run is resumed via any of the three entry paths (--resume flag, auto-resume on status=interrupted, or zbuild pipeline resume --run-id) — Then: The completed stage's artifacts appear in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR byte-identical to their state at the time of interruption — And: No stage.start event is emitted for the completed stage
- [#1805/RHYD-2] A complete stage whose primary artifact cannot be rehydrated causes exit 1 before any stage.start event is emitted — Given: A run is being resumed; a stage is marked complete in persisted state; its primary artifact is absent from both disk and the git state branch after rehydration attempt — When: The runner processes that stage during resume rehydration — Then: The runner exits 1 — And: No stage.start event has been emitted for any stage
- [#1805/FSTG-1] --from-stage <s> rehydrates all stages before <s> and dispatches <s> as the first stage — Given: A previous run completed stages before <s>; their artifacts are present in the git state branch; a new invocation uses --from-stage <s> — When: The runner starts with --from-stage <s> — Then: The artifacts from every stage before <s> appear in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR before the dispatch loop starts — And: Stage <s> is dispatched as the first stage (a stage.start event is emitted for <s>) — And: No stage.start event is emitted for any stage before <s>
- [#1805/FSTG-2] --from-stage <s> when a prior stage has no restorable artifact emits a diagnostic and exits 1 before any stage.start event — Given: --from-stage <s> is active; at least one stage before <s> has no restorable primary artifact in the git state branch — When: The runner performs the from-stage preflight check — Then: The diagnostic phrase "has no restorable primary artifact" appears on stderr — And: The runner exits 1 before any stage.start event is emitted
- [#1805/AMDR-1] ADR-006-resume-contract.md amended with step 3.6 (rehydrate completed-stage artifacts before dispatch loop; absent artifact causes exit 1; ordering constraint: not to be combined with dispatch-loop changes); enforcing test names (resume-rehydrate-test.sh, resume-entry-points-test.sh) added inline
- [#1805/AMDR-2] ADR-050-prior-work-reuse-contract.md §6 amended with boundary note: the invariant "never skip a stage on prior output" applies to new runs; a resume continues the same run and is governed by ADR-006
- [#1805/ITER-1] Cycle orchestrator reads current_iter from persisted state on resume and starts the iteration loop from that value; fresh runs and nested-loop re-entries always start at iter=1 — Given: A run is being resumed; persisted state records cycle_iterations[CYCLE_ID].current_iter=2 (iter 1 completed before interruption); _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true is exported — When: The cycle orchestrator's run body executes — Then: The iteration loop starts at iter 2, not iter 1 — And: No stage.start event is emitted for any iter-1 stage — And: When _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE is false or unset (fresh run or nested-loop re-entry), the loop starts at iter=1
- [#1805/DSPK-1] On resume, stage k (the interrupted stage) is dispatched and emits stage.start — Given: A run with stages 1…N was interrupted during stage k; stages 1…k-1 are marked complete with their artifacts present in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR after rehydration — When: The dispatch loop reaches stage k during resume — Then: Stage k emits a stage.start event
- [#1805/ENTR-1] All three resume entry paths (--resume flag, auto-resume on status=interrupted, zbuild pipeline resume --run-id) restore completed-stage artifacts before the dispatch loop — Given: A run has been interrupted and its state is persisted in runs/<run_id>/ — When: The run is resumed via any of the three entry paths in turn — Then: Completed-stage artifacts appear in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR before any stage.start event is emitted, for each of the three entry paths independently — And: No stage.start event is emitted for any stage marked complete in the interrupted run's state
- [#1805/FRSH-1] A fresh run dispatches all stages from stage 1 with no stage skipped due to prior state and no prior-run artifacts in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR
- [#1805/DLGT-1] The hydrate plugin's hydrate_run calls _artifact_persist_put_back so artifacts placed by the resume path appear at the same filesystem paths as those a hydrate run would produce — Given: hydrate_run is about to execute; _artifact_persist_put_back is overridden in the test environment with a sentinel-writing function — When: hydrate_run executes — Then: The sentinel file is written, confirming hydrate_run reached _artifact_persist_put_back
- [#1805/CYCL-1] The test fixtures used by resume-rehydrate-test.sh and from-stage-rehydrate-test.sh each contain a pipeline stage of type: cycle, verified by an assert_contains tagged [#1805/CYCL-1] in each file, ensuring RESU-1 through FROM-1 tests run against a cyclic pipeline
